explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM-based BRI metric against human evaluation by correlating human preference scores with various metrics including BRI, showing BRI has stronger correlation with human judgment

prompts.notes: Chain-of-thought prompts for LLM questioner shown in Appendix A, filtering process prompts described but exact text not fully provided

guidelines.notes: Detailed evaluation instructions provided to human testers including scenario description and specific questions about effectiveness and efficiency

sample_size.notes: 60 instances were presented to each of the 30 human testers for evaluation

quantitative_scores.notes: Results presented in Table show BRI is significantly more strongly correlated with human preference than Recall, MRR, NDCG, and Hits metrics

validation_results.summary_finding: BRI metric shows significantly stronger correlation with human preference compared to existing metrics (Recall, MRR, NDCG, Hits), demonstrating better alignment with human judgment for interactive retrieval systems.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLMs used for question generation and filtering, while BRI metric (validated against human preference) evaluates overall system performance based on effectiveness and efficiency criteria also evaluated by humans
